subject: Emotions
title: The Marshmallow Test Revisited
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Marshmallow Test Revisited.

hook.text: A 4-year-old stares at a marshmallow. Wait 15 minutes, get two. Most kids grab it. The ones who wait do better in life.

buildup.text: Walter Mischel's 1972 study followed those kids for decades. Delayers had higher SAT scores and lower BMI.

discovery.text: The key wasn't willpower. Successful kids used strategies: looking away, singing, reframing the treat as a cloud.

twist.text: Recent replications show wealth matters: kids from stable homes wait longer. It's trust, not just self-control.

climax.text: The marshmallow test isn't about resisting temptation. It's about having strategies and a safe environment.

punchline.text: Self-control isn't a muscle. It's a strategy born of safety.

quiz.question: What did recent replications of the marshmallow test reveal?
